auraIntro: Explorer, Pinwheel Galaxy is an immense face-on spiral galaxy containing over 1 trillion stars and 3,000 starbirth regions.
overview: The Pinwheel Galaxy (M101 or NGC 5457) is a massive face-on spiral galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major, roughly 21 million light-years from Earth.
formation: Formed approximately 13.1 billion years ago, tidal interactions with nearby companion galaxies asymmetricized its outer arms and accelerated starbirth.
structure: A face-on grand spiral galaxy spanning 170,000 light-years—nearly double the size of the Milky Way—with a stellar mass of 1 trillion solar masses.
discoveryHistory: Discovered by Pierre Méchain on March 27, 1781, and cataloged by Charles Messier.
observationTips: Due to its face-on orientation, surface brightness is low; requires dark skies and 8-inch or larger optics to resolve individual arm nodes.
funFacts: Contains over 3,000 giant H II regions where active star formation creates massive newborn star clusters.
Nearly twice the diameter of our Milky Way Galaxy, holding an estimated 1 trillion stars.
Hosted supernova SN 2023ixf in May 2023, one of the brightest and closest Type Ia supernovae seen in two decades.

cards.body: In May 2023, Japanese amateur astronomer Koichi Itagaki discovered supernova SN 2023ixf in M101's spiral arms, attracting worldwide observation.
bulletPoints: SN 2023ixf occurred when a red supergiant star collapsed into a neutron star.
M101 holds 3,000+ ionized hydrogen H II regions.
